title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous pages. X is a scheme of finite type over Q-bar, with a descent datum. G_X is a profinite group of 'semilinear' symmetries of X that maps onto (an open subgroup of) Gamma = Gal(Q-bar/Q). E_X is the corresponding extension 1 -> pi_1(X) -> E_X -> G_X -> 1, the arithmetic fundamental group twisted by extra automorphisms.

On the previous page, a point xi in X(Q-bar) gives the following. Over an open subgroup Gamma' of Gamma there is a lifting Gamma' -> G_X that fixes xi, i.e. factors through the stabilizer G_X(xi). Functoriality of pi_1 at the point xi then gives a homomorphism phi_xi : Gamma' -> E_X compatible with the projections. It is defined up to pi_1(X)-conjugation.

This page. (a) Grothendieck stresses that only the GERM of phi_xi is well defined, i.e. modulo restriction to finite-index subgroups. So the invariant is eta_xi in lim_{Gamma' in Gamma} Hom_{G_X}(Gamma', E_X) / pi_1-conjugation; this is formula (11).

(b) A bracketed remark: if X maps injectively into an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (a semi-abelian variety, i.e. a generalized Albanese/Jacobian), then xi is known once its germ is known. Indeed already the image of eta_xi in a suitable abelian H^1 suffices, namely the Kummer class in H^1(Gamma', T(G)). This is the injectivity half of the section conjecture, proved by the Kummer-map argument: G(K) is finitely generated (Mordell-Weil plus Dirichlet units for the torus part), so G(K) -> H^1(K, T G) is injective. Passing to smaller Gamma' preserves injectivity because T(G)^{Gamma_L} = 0.

(c) Paragraph 4, formulas (12)-(13). Let D = sum_{i in I} D_i be an effective reduced divisor with normal crossings, with X regular at the generic point of each D_i. Put X' = X - supp D. Consider the subgroup G_{X;D} of G_X preserving D; by abuse of notation it is written G_{X'}, or more precisely G_{X'}(I). This gives the extension (14) 1 -> pi_1(X') -> E_{X'} -> G_{X'} -> 1 on the next page.

The next page then supplies three things:
- an action G_{X'} -> S_I on the components;
- Kummer-theoretic exterior homomorphisms Z-hat(1) -> pi_1(X'), the inertia at each D_i;
- compatibility of these with the cyclotomic character.

This is the setup for 'cuspidal' or boundary sections and inertia data, generalizing cusps of curves to normal-crossing boundaries in higher dimension. Overall the problem served is the arithmetic (anabelian) description of rational points via sections of fundamental-group extensions, in the framework of 'paradigmes des courbes algébriques' with extra symmetry groups G_X.
errors: (11) as written omits the conditions that the homomorphisms lift the given Gamma' -> G_X and are taken modulo pi_1(X)-conjugation. The page itself is sloppy here, with Hom/Ext crossings-out.

The injectivity claim needs the Kummer map on the semi-abelian variety to be injective over every number field and stable under restriction to open subgroups. This holds (Mordell-Weil plus finiteness of torsion, so T(G)^{Gamma_L} = 0), but it is not argued on the page.

ideas.what: A rational/algebraic point gives a germ of section Gamma' -> E_X of the fundamental-group extension, defined only up to restriction to open subgroups and pi_1-conjugation, with G_X a group of semilinear automorphisms rather than just Galois
ideas.modern_name: section map X(K) -> {sections of pi_1 exact sequence}; equivariant/orbifold version with automorphism group
ideas.where_published: Brief an Faltings (27.6.1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: If X embeds in a semi-abelian variety, a point is determined by (the abelianized image of) its section germ
ideas.modern_name: injectivity part of the section conjecture via Kummer map / Albanese
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1983 letter; standard (e.g. Mochizuki, Nakamura, Stix's book)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (statement for hyperbolic curves)

ideas.what: Open complement of a normal-crossings divisor, the stabilizer subgroup of the divisor, and Kummer inertia homomorphisms Z-hat(1) -> pi_1(X') per component, compatible with the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: log/tame fundamental group, inertia at boundary divisors, cuspidal sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 / Grothendieck-Murre (tame pi_1); cuspidal sections: Nakamura, Stix

missed.claim: The 'germ of section attached to a point' formalism, with injectivity via embedding in a semi-abelian variety, is written down here around 1980-81, apparently earlier than the 1983 Faltings letter usually cited as the origin of the section conjecture. It is set for varieties of finite type with an extra symmetry group G_X, not just Galois.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical dating of the section conjecture's prehistory. The equivariant/G_X-twisted variant (sections over stabilizers of points) is rarely treated in the section-conjecture literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically routine (Kummer-map injectivity, tame inertia at an NC boundary). The interest is mainly historical: an early (c. 1980-81) formulation of section germs attached to points, in an equivariant setting.
